
```{r setup for stan}
library(tidyverse)
library(ggrepel)
library(bayesplot)
library(tidybayes)
library(cmdstanr)
library(loo)
options(mc.cores = 4)

dir.create("rdata", recursive = TRUE, showWarnings = FALSE)
```


```{r reading in similarities}

trial_info = read_csv("../data/trial_info.csv") %>% 
  filter(!str_detect(Condition, "Filler")) 

sim_by_layer_timeseries = read_csv("../audio_similarities/incremental_dtw_similarities_by_layer.csv")

sim_by_layer_tw = sim_by_layer_timeseries %>% 
  left_join(onsets_w, by = c("fileA" = "word")) %>% 
  mutate(tw = case_when(
    between(time, 0, Onset_t1) ~ "t0",
    between(time, Onset_t1, Offset_t1) ~ "t1",
    between(time, Onset_t2, Offset_t2) ~ "t2",
    between(time, Onset_t3, Offset_t3) ~ "t3")) %>% 
  filter(!is.na(tw)) %>% 
  group_by(fileA, fileB, layer, tw) %>% 
  summarize(mean_sim = mean(similarity, na.rm = T))

```
```{r plot of dtw similarity timeseries}
beaker_onsets = onsets_w %>% filter(word == "beaker")

p_sims<-ggplot(sim_by_layer_timeseries %>% 
         filter(fileA == "beaker", fileB == "speaker", layer > 0))+

           color = "darkgrey" )+
  geom_vline(aes(xintercept = beaker_onsets %>% pull(Offset_t3)), linetype = "dashed",
           color = "darkgrey" )+
  annotate(geom = "text", 
           x = ((beaker_onsets %>% pull(Onset_t1))/2),
           y = 0.76,
           label = "t0")+
  annotate(geom = "text", 
           x = beaker_onsets %>% pull(Onset_t1) + ((beaker_onsets %>% pull(Duration_t1))/2),
           y = 0.76,
           label = "t1" )+
  annotate(geom = "text",

         filter(fileA == "beaker", fileB == "speaker", 
                layer %in% c(1, 10, 20, 30, 40, 47)))+
  stat_summary(aes(x = tw, y = mean_sim, color = layer, group = layer), geom = "line", linewidth = 1)+
  stat_summary(aes(x = tw, y = mean_sim, color = layer, group=layer), geom = "point", size = 3)+
  scale_color_viridis_c(direction = -1, option = "turbo")+
  labs(y = "Mean Cosine Similarity", x = "Time window")+
```

```{r prepping ET data for Stan format}

# prepping ET data for Stan format

ET_dur_data_4t_crit2 = ET_dur_data_4t %>% 
  filter(!Condition %in% c("Filler 1","Filler 2","Filler 3","Practice")) %>% 
  left_join(ET_quality_by_trial, by = c("subjID", "BlockOrder","trial_nums")) %>% 
  filter(click_correct ==1,
         subjID %in% keep_subjects,
         prop_tracked >= .5) %>% 
  left_join(trial_info, by = c("ItemNum", "Condition")) %>% 
  mutate( TL_role = case_when(
    TL == Pic1 ~ "target",
    TL == Pic2 ~ "competitor",
    TL == Pic3 ~ "dist1",
    TL == Pic4 ~ "dist2"
  ),
  TR_role = case_when(
    TR == Pic1 ~ "target",
    TR == Pic2 ~ "competitor",
    TR == Pic3 ~ "dist1",
    TR == Pic4 ~ "dist2"
  ),
  BL_role = case_when(
    BL == Pic1 ~ "target",
    BL == Pic2 ~ "competitor",
    BL == Pic3 ~ "dist1",
    BL == Pic4 ~ "dist2"
  ),
  BR_role = case_when(
    BR == Pic1 ~ "target",
    BR == Pic2 ~ "competitor",
    BR == Pic3 ~ "dist1",
    BR == Pic4 ~ "dist2"
  ),
  target_dur2 = if_else(
    gaze_location == 'TL' & TL_role == "target" |
      gaze_location == 'TR' & TR_role == "target" |
      gaze_location == 'BL' & BL_role == "target" |
      gaze_location == 'BR' & BR_role == "target",
    event_dur, 0
  ),
  compet_dur = if_else(
    gaze_location == 'TL' & TL_role == "competitor" |
      gaze_location == 'TR' & TR_role == "competitor" |
      gaze_location == 'BL' & BL_role == "competitor" |
      gaze_location == 'BR' & BR_role == "competitor",
    event_dur, 0
  ),
  dist1_dur = if_else(
    gaze_location == 'TL' & TL_role == "dist1" |
      gaze_location == 'TR' & TR_role == "dist1" |
      gaze_location == 'BL' & BL_role == "dist1" |
      gaze_location == 'BR' & BR_role == "dist1",
    event_dur, 0
  ),
  dist2_dur = if_else(
    gaze_location == 'TL' & TL_role == "dist2" |
      gaze_location == 'TR' & TR_role == "dist2" |
      gaze_location == 'BL' & BL_role == "dist2" |
      gaze_location == 'BR' & BR_role == "dist2",
    event_dur, 0
  ),
  BlockType = case_when(
    BlockOrder == "b0" & BlockCond == "intact" ~ 1,
    BlockOrder == "b0" & BlockCond == "noisy" ~ 2,
    BlockOrder == "b1" & BlockCond == "noisy" ~ 3,
    BlockOrder == "b1" & BlockCond == "intact" & EXPT == "noEA" ~ 4,
    BlockOrder == "b1" & BlockCond == "intact" & EXPT == "EA" ~ 5,
    TRUE ~ 9999
  )
  ) %>% 
  group_by(BlockType, tw, subjID, trial_nums, BlockOrder, BlockNum.x, TrialOrder, ItemNum, Target.x, Cohort.x, Rhyme.x, Pic1, Pic2, Pic3, Pic4, Condition, total_dur) %>% 
  summarize(sum_target_dur = sum(target_dur2),
            sum_compet_dur = sum(compet_dur),
            sum_dist1_dur = sum(dist1_dur),
            sum_dist2_dur = sum(dist2_dur)) %>% 
  mutate(target_prop = sum_target_dur/total_dur,
         compet_prop = sum_compet_dur/total_dur,
         dist1_prop = sum_dist1_dur/total_dur,
         dist2_prop = sum_dist2_dur/total_dur
  ) %>% 
  arrange(subjID, BlockOrder, TrialOrder, tw)

# Squeeze the proportions to avoid exact 0s and 1s (Dirichlet requirement)
squeeze <- function(x) { (x * 0.999) + 0.0005 }

ET_data_by_items_conds_tws = ET_dur_data_4t_crit2 %>% 
  group_by(ItemNum, Condition, BlockType, tw, Pic1, Pic2, Pic3, Pic4) %>% 
  summarize(mean_target_prop = mean(target_prop), 
            mean_compet_prop = mean(compet_prop), 
            mean_dist1_prop = mean(dist1_prop),
            mean_dist2_prop = mean(dist2_prop)) %>% 
  #left_join(trial_info, by = c("ItemNum", "Condition")) %>% 
  mutate(sim_target = 1-1e-7) %>% 
  full_join(sim_by_layer_tw, 
            by = c("Pic1" = "fileA", "Pic2" = "fileB", "tw" = "tw"),
            relationship = "many-to-many") %>% 
  rename(sim_compet = mean_sim) %>% 
  full_join(sim_by_layer_tw, 
            by = c("Pic1" = "fileA", "Pic3" = "fileB", "tw" = "tw", "layer" = "layer")) %>%
  rename(sim_dist1 = mean_sim) %>% 
  full_join(sim_by_layer_tw, 
            by = c("Pic1" = "fileA", "Pic4" = "fileB", "tw" = "tw", "layer" = "layer")) %>%
  rename(sim_dist2 = mean_sim) %>% 
  filter( !is.na(ItemNum)) %>%  # NAs added during joining
  mutate(sq_target = squeeze(mean_target_prop),
         sq_comp = squeeze(mean_compet_prop),
         sq_dist1 = squeeze(mean_dist1_prop),
         sq_dist2 = squeeze(mean_dist2_prop),
         total_sq = sq_target + sq_comp + sq_dist1 + sq_dist2,
         y_col1 = sq_target / total_sq, # normalizing
         y_col2 = sq_comp / total_sq,
         y_col3 = sq_dist1 / total_sq,
         y_col4 = 1 - (y_col1 + y_col2 + y_col3) # forcing cols to add up to 1 for dirichlet (floating point problems)
         ) %>% 
  arrange(layer, BlockType, ItemNum, Condition, tw ) 
```

```{r, eval = F}
model <- cmdstan_model("stan_files/model_log_domain_weak_priors.stan") 
```


```{r loop over layers, eval = F}
# loop through sims for all layers to see which layer's similarity values fit data best

num_layers <- max(ET_data_by_items_conds_tws$layer)
loo_results <- list()

# Loop through all layers
for (L in 1:num_layers) {
  
  print(paste("Fitting Layer", L))
  
  ET_data_by_items_conds_tws_1layer = ET_data_by_items_conds_tws %>% 
  filter(layer == L)

  
    # 5. Bind it together
    y_matrix_L <- cbind(ET_data_by_items_conds_tws_1layer$y_col1, 
                      ET_data_by_items_conds_tws_1layer$y_col2, 
                      ET_data_by_items_conds_tws_1layer$y_col3, 
                      ET_data_by_items_conds_tws_1layer$y_col4)
    
    # 3. Create the Similarity Matrix
    sim_matrix_L <- cbind(
      ET_data_by_items_conds_tws_1layer$sim_target,
      ET_data_by_items_conds_tws_1layer$sim_compet,
      ET_data_by_items_conds_tws_1layer$sim_dist1,
      ET_data_by_items_conds_tws_1layer$sim_dist2
    )
    
    # create the data list
    stan_data_L <- list(
      N = nrow(ET_data_by_items_conds_tws_1layer),
      sim = sim_matrix_L,
      timestep = parse_number(ET_data_by_items_conds_tws_1layer$tw)+1,
      y = y_matrix_L,
      num_groups = max(ET_data_by_items_conds_tws_1layer$BlockType),
      group_id = ET_data_by_items_conds_tws_1layer$BlockType
    )
  
  # Fit the model
  fit_L <- model$sample(data = stan_data_L, chains = 4, refresh = 0)
  
  # Extract the pointwise log-likelihood and compute LOO
  layer_log_lik_matrix <- fit_L$draws("log_lik", format = "matrix")
  layer_loo <- loo(layer_log_lik_matrix)
  
  # Store the result
  loo_results[[L]] <- layer_loo
}

saveRDS(loo_results,"rdata/loo_results2_21102026.rds")
```

```{r loop over layers with generic similarities, eval = F}
    # 5. Bind it together

                      ET_data_by_items_conds_tws_1layer_g$y_col3, 
                      ET_data_by_items_conds_tws_1layer_g$y_col4)
    
    # 3. Create the Similarity Matrix
    sim_matrix_g_L <- cbind(
      ET_data_by_items_conds_tws_1layer_g$sim_generic_target,
      ET_data_by_items_conds_tws_1layer_g$sim_generic_compet,
      ET_data_by_items_conds_tws_1layer_g$sim_generic_dist1,
      ET_data_by_items_conds_tws_1layer_g$sim_generic_dist2
    )
    
    # create the data list
    stan_data_g_L <- list(
      N = nrow(ET_data_by_items_conds_tws_1layer_g),

  # Fit the model
```

(ref:hubert-plot-caption) Acoustic analysis pipeline. **(A)** The HuBERT model was used to incrementally extract embeddings across layers for target, competitor, and distractor audio. Audio files were annotated for four time windows of interest (t0 = pre-noun, t1 = onset of noun to disambiguation, t2 = onset of disambiguating phoneme to offset of disambiguating phoneme, t3 = offset of disambiguating phoneme to offset of noun). Pairs of audio stimuli were aligned using dynamic time warping. **(B)** Cosine similarity was calculated per frame for each layer. Similarity timeseries for "beaker"-"speaker" pair is shown. Time windows are based on the timestamps of "beaker." **(C)** Cosine similarities were then averaged within four time windows of interest (t0, t1, t2, t3) for each layer (subset of layers shown for clarity) in order to be used for fitting to eye-tracking data.  **(D)** Performance of the model in predicting eye-tracking data was compared across HuBERT layers. Orange point indicates the layer that led to the best performance. The gray ribbon indicates the 2 x standard error of the difference in ELPD relative to the best performing layer.

```{r hubert-plot, fig.cap = "(ref:hubert-plot-caption)", fig.width = 8, fig.height = 5, dpi = 300}

p_pipeline_image_final <- free(p_pipeline_image, side = "l")

layout_design <- "
  AAA
  BCD
"

pipeline_layout <- wrap_plots(
  A = p_pipeline_image_final, 
  B = p_sims,
  C = p_sims_tw,
  D = p_layers, 
  design = layout_design
```

```{r posterior preds from generic model}
# Extract the predicted_posterior matrix
# This returns a dataframe with columns like: predicted_posterior[1,1], predicted_posterior[1,2]...
pred_summary <- fit_avg_g$summary("predicted_posterior", "mean", quantile, .args = list(probs = c(0.025, .975)))

# Reshape the Stan output into a N x 4 matrix
pred_df <- pred_summary %>%
  #mutate(type = str_sub(variable,1,1)) %>% 
  mutate(
    # Extract the row (n) and column (i) indices from the variable name
    row_idx = as.numeric(str_extract(variable, "(?<=\\[)\\d+")),
    col_idx = as.numeric(str_extract(variable, "\\d+(?=\\])"))
  ) %>%
  arrange(col_idx, row_idx) # arrange by the variable name to ensure the rows match 

mean_matrix <- pred_df %>% pull(mean) %>%
  matrix(nrow = nrow(ET_data_by_items_conds_tws_avglayer_g), ncol = 4)
q2.5_matrix <- pred_df %>% pull(`2.5%`) %>%
  matrix(nrow = nrow(ET_data_by_items_conds_tws_avglayer_g), ncol = 4)
q97.5_matrix <- pred_df %>% pull(`97.5%`) %>%
  matrix(nrow = nrow(ET_data_by_items_conds_tws_avglayer_g), ncol = 4)

# Bind the predictions back to original dataframe
ET_data_by_items_conds_tws_avglayer_g_w_posts <- ET_data_by_items_conds_tws_avglayer_g
ET_data_by_items_conds_tws_avglayer_g_w_posts$pred_target_m = mean_matrix[, 1]
ET_data_by_items_conds_tws_avglayer_g_w_posts$pred_competitor_m = mean_matrix[, 2] # Cohort, Rhyme, or Distractor 1
ET_data_by_items_conds_tws_avglayer_g_w_posts$pred_distractor1_m = mean_matrix[, 3]
ET_data_by_items_conds_tws_avglayer_g_w_posts$pred_distractor2_m = mean_matrix[, 4]
  
ET_data_by_items_conds_tws_avglayer_g_w_posts$pred_target_lb = q2.5_matrix[, 1]
ET_data_by_items_conds_tws_avglayer_g_w_posts$pred_competitor_lb = q2.5_matrix[, 2] # Cohort, Rhyme, or Distractor 1
ET_data_by_items_conds_tws_avglayer_g_w_posts$pred_distractor1_lb = q2.5_matrix[, 3]
ET_data_by_items_conds_tws_avglayer_g_w_posts$pred_distractor2_lb = q2.5_matrix[, 4]

ET_data_by_items_conds_tws_avglayer_g_w_posts$pred_target_ub = q97.5_matrix[, 1]
ET_data_by_items_conds_tws_avglayer_g_w_posts$pred_competitor_ub = q97.5_matrix[, 2] # Cohort, Rhyme, or Distractor 1
ET_data_by_items_conds_tws_avglayer_g_w_posts$pred_distractor1_ub = q97.5_matrix[, 3]
ET_data_by_items_conds_tws_avglayer_g_w_posts$pred_distractor2_ub = q97.5_matrix[, 4]
```



```{r}
long_data = ET_data_by_items_conds_tws_avglayer_g_w_posts %>% 
  rowid_to_column("row") %>% 
  rename(
    y_1    = y_col1,          pred_1 = pred_target_m,
    y_2    = y_col2,          pred_2 = pred_competitor_m,
    y_3    = y_col3,          pred_3 = pred_distractor1_m,
    y_4    = y_col4,          pred_4 = pred_distractor2_m,
  ) %>%
  # pivot using .value to split the prefix from the index number
  pivot_longer(
    cols = c(y_1:y_4, pred_1:pred_4),
    names_to = c(".value", "ROI"),
    names_pattern = "(y|pred)_(.)"
  ) %>% 
  mutate(ROIname = case_when(
    ROI == 1 ~ "target",
    ROI == 2 ~ "compet.",
    ROI == 3 | ROI == 4 ~ "dist."
  ))

long_data$ROIname = factor(long_data$ROIname, levels = c("target", "compet.", "dist."))
long_data$Condition = factor(long_data$Condition, levels = c("No competition", "Cohort competition", "Rhyme competition"))

```

```{r get draws, eval = FALSE}
saveRDS(post_preds, "rdata/posterior_preds_stan_fit_avg_g_21102026.rds")
```

(ref:model-posteriors-plot-caption) Eye-tracking data across four timewindows of interest and model posterior summary. **(A)** Timecourse of proportion of eye fixations to targets and competitors downsampled to four time windows in the No competition and Early competition conditions. **(B)** Timecourse of proportion of eye fixations to targets and competitors downsampled to four time windows in the No competition and Late competition conditions. **(C)** Posterior model predictions (50 posterior draws) over four time windows by ROI (target and competitor/distractor) in the No competition and Early competition conditions. **(D)** Posterior model predictions (50 posterior draws) over four time windows by ROI (target and competitor/distractor) in the No competition and Late competition conditions. **(E)** Correlation between posterior model predictions and average eye fixation proportions: points represent means per competition condition, time window, and ROI (labels indicate the ROI and time window). Black line indicates identity line. In A-D, solid lines indicate target fixations. Dashed lines indicate competitor or distractor fixations.

```{r extracting condition means and CrIs for contrasts of interest}
post_means_CrIs_tw_diff = post_preds_summary_tw_only %>% 
  pivot_wider( names_from = c(ROIname, tw), values_from = pred) %>% 
  mutate(t0_TA = target_t0 - compet._t0,
         t1_TA = target_t1 - compet._t1,
         t2_TA = target_t2 - compet._t2,
         t3_TA = target_t3 - compet._t3) %>% 
  summarize(across(
      .cols = -c(.draw), 
      .fns = list(
        m = ~ mean(.x, na.rm = TRUE),
        q2.5 = ~ quantile(.x, 0.025, na.rm = TRUE),
        q97.5 = ~ quantile(.x, 0.975, na.rm = TRUE),
        q5 = ~ quantile(.x, 0.05, na.rm = TRUE),
        q95 = ~ quantile(.x, 0.95, na.rm = TRUE),
        abovezero = ~ mean(.x>0, na.rm=TRUE)
      ),
      .names = "{.col}_{.fn}"
    )

  pivot_longer(
    cols = everything(), 
    names_to = c("variable", ".value"),
    names_pattern = "(.*)_(.*)$"

  mutate(
    across(where(is.numeric), ~ round(.x, digits = 2))
```

```{r plotting tau}

tau_draws <- fit_avg_g %>%
  spread_draws(tau[group_id])

tau_draws <- tau_draws %>%
  mutate(
    block_name = case_when(
      group_id == 1 ~ "Intact [1st block]",
      group_id == 2 ~ "Noisy [1st block]",
      group_id == 3 ~ "Noisy after Intact [2nd block]",
      group_id == 4 ~ "Intact after Noisy, no explanation [2nd block]",
      group_id == 5 ~ "Intact after Noisy, w/ explanation [2nd block]"
    ),
    block_name = factor(block_name, levels = rev(c(
      "Intact [1st block]",
      "Noisy [1st block]",
      "Noisy after Intact [2nd block]",
      "Intact after Noisy, no explanation [2nd block]",
      "Intact after Noisy, w/ explanation [2nd block]"
    )))
  )


tau_plot<-ggplot(tau_draws, aes(x = tau, y = block_name, fill = block_name)) +
  stat_halfeye(
    alpha = 0.7,
    .width = c(0.68, 0.95), 
    point_interval = median_qi 
  ) +
  scale_fill_viridis_d(option = "mako", guide = "none") +
  labs(
    x = expression("Estimated Noise (" * tau * ")"),
    y = NULL
  ) +
  theme_classic(base_size = 14) +
  theme(
    axis.text.y = element_text(face = "bold", size = 12)
  )

```
```{r plotting tau contrasts}
# real initial_noise_effect = tau[2] - tau[1];
#   real noise_residual_effect = tau[4] - tau[1];
#   real noise_contrast_effect = tau[3] - tau[2];
#   real explain_away_effect = tau[5] - tau[4]; 
#   real explained_noise_residual_effect = tau[5] - tau[1]; 

contrast_draws <- fit_avg_g %>%
  spread_draws(initial_noise_effect, noise_residual_effect, noise_contrast_effect, explain_away_effect, explained_noise_residual_effect) %>%
  tidyr::pivot_longer(
    cols = c(initial_noise_effect, noise_residual_effect, noise_contrast_effect, explain_away_effect, explained_noise_residual_effect),
    names_to = "contrast_name",
    values_to = "difference"
  ) %>%
  mutate(
    contrast_label = case_when(
      contrast_name == "initial_noise_effect" ~ "Noise effect:\nNoisy [1st block] - Intact [1st block]",
      contrast_name == "noise_residual_effect" ~ "Adaptation effect:\nIntact, no explanation [2nd block] - Intact [1st block]",
      contrast_name == "noise_contrast_effect" ~ "Adaptation effect:\nNoisy [2nd block] - Noisy [1st block]",
      contrast_name == "explain_away_effect" ~ "Explaining away effect:\nIntact w/ explanation [2nd block] - Intact, no explanation [2nd block]",
      contrast_name == "explained_noise_residual_effect" ~ "Intact, w/ explanation [2nd block] - Intact [1st block]"
    ),
    contrast_label = factor(contrast_label, levels = rev(c(
      "Noise effect:\nNoisy [1st block] - Intact [1st block]",
      "Adaptation effect:\nIntact, no explanation [2nd block] - Intact [1st block]",
      "Adaptation effect:\nNoisy [2nd block] - Noisy [1st block]",
      "Explaining away effect:\nIntact w/ explanation [2nd block] - Intact, no explanation [2nd block]",
      "Intact, w/ explanation [2nd block] - Intact [1st block]"
    )))
  )


contrast_plot<-ggplot(contrast_draws %>% filter(contrast_label != "Intact, w/ explanation [2nd block] - Intact [1st block]"), 
       aes(x = difference, y = contrast_label)) +
  geom_vline(xintercept = 0, linetype = "dashed", color = "firebrick", linewidth = 1) +
  stat_halfeye(
    alpha = 0.8,
    fill = "steelblue",
    .width = c(0.68, 0.95),
    point_interval = median_qi
  ) +
  labs(
    x = expression("Difference in " * tau * ""),
    y = NULL
  ) +
  theme_classic(base_size = 14) +
  theme(
    axis.text.y = element_text(face = "bold", size = 11)
  )
```

(ref:tau-effects-plot-caption) The effect of the manipulation of noise in the environment. **(A)** Posterior predictions (50 draws) of the timecourse of proportion of eye fixations to targets and competitors across competition conditions by block condition (*Intact* blocks vs. *Noisy* blocks). **(B)** Posterior of the listener's noise estimate, $\tau$, per block condition. **(C)** Posterior estimates of differences between $\tau$ values across blocks. Points indicate medians, and intervals are 68% (thicker lines) and 95% (thinner lines).

## Model selection and layer-wise analysis

To fit the Bayesian model to the eye-tracking data and estimate $\tau$ values across different block conditions, the eye-tracking data were first downsampled to four time windows of interest and then averaged across participants for each item and condition (Figure\ \@ref(fig:model-posteriors-plots)A-B). Proportions of fixations to all four regions of interest (ROIs) were simultaneously modeled with a Dirichlet distribution. Given that the similarity timeseries differed across layers (Figure\ \@ref(fig:hubert-plot)B), we evaluated several versions of the noise likelihood to determine the granularity of information that best predicted eye-gaze. Model performance was compared using leave-one-out cross-validation to estimate expected log-pointwise predictive density (ELPD-LOO). A difference in ELPD was considered significant if it exceeded two times the standard error of the ELPD difference between models [@sivula2025Uncertainty]. 
Models built on *stimulus-specific* similarities were compared against those using *generic* similarities (i.e., averaging target-candidate similarity for a given condition across all stimulus pairs).
First, a series of models were fitted with stimulus-specific similarities from each HuBERT layer. Layer `r best_layer` yielded the best performance, with `r num_tied_layers-1` other layers (ranging from `r min_tied_layer` to `r max_tied_layer`) with only nominally lower ELPDs. 
Then, a model using stimulus-specific similarities averaged across all `r num_tied_layers` best-fitting layers was fitted. 
Next, the layer-wise evaluation was repeated using generic similarities. Layer `r best_g_layer` led to significantly better performance than all other layers (Figure\ \@ref(fig:hubert-plot)D). 
A hybrid model using generic similarities averaged across the `r num_tied_layers` layers found using the stimulus-specific similarities was also fit for direct comparison with the stimulus-specific model.

Performance was lower for the model using stimulus-specific similarities averaging across `r num_tied_layers` layers ($\text{ELPD-LOO} =$ `r elpd_comparison["model1",]["elpd_loo"]`, $SE_{\text{ELPD-LOO}} =$ `r elpd_comparison["model1",]["se_elpd_loo"]`) compared to the model with generic similarities from layer `r best_g_layer` ($\text{ELPD-LOO} =$ `r elpd_comparison["model3",]["elpd_loo"]`, $SE_{\text{ELPD-LOO}} =$ `r elpd_comparison["model3",]["se_elpd_loo"]`, $\Delta =$ `r elpd_comparison_item_v_avg_g[2,]["elpd_diff"]`, $SE_{\Delta} =$ `r elpd_comparison_item_v_avg_g[2,]["se_diff"]`) and the model with generic similarities averaging across `r num_tied_layers` layers ($\text{ELPD-LOO} =$ `r elpd_comparison["model2",]["elpd_loo"]`, $SE_{\text{ELPD-LOO}} =$ `r elpd_comparison["model2",]["se_elpd_loo"]`, $\Delta =$ `r elpd_comparison_item_v_g[2,]["elpd_diff"]`, $SE_{\Delta} =$ `r elpd_comparison_item_v_g[2,]["se_diff"]`). The model using generic similarities from layer `r best_g_layer` performed better than that which averaged over layers ($\Delta =$ `r elpd_comparison_g_v_avg_g[2,]["elpd_diff"]`, $SE_{\Delta} =$ `r elpd_comparison_g_v_avg_g[2,]["se_diff"]`) and was adopted for further analyses.



## Bayesian noisy-channel belief updating model captures the timecourse of eye-gaze during speech perception 

The posterior distribution of this best-fitting model is summarized in Figure\ \@ref(fig:model-posteriors-plots)C-D. To summarize the results, I report means ($M$) of the posterior samples as point estimates of conditions or differences ($\Delta$) between conditions along with 95% posterior credible intervals ($95\%~\text{CrI}$) of those estimates.

Across conditions and blocks, the model predicts that fixations to the target increase as the stimulus unfolds (t0: $M=$ `r t0_target_m`, 
$95\%~\text{CrI}=$ [`r t0_target_q2.5`, `r t0_target_q97.5`]; 
t1: $M=$ `r t1_target_m`, 
$95\%~\text{CrI}=$ [`r t1_target_q2.5`, `r t1_target_q97.5`];
t2: $M=$ `r t2_target_m`, 
$95\%~\text{CrI}=$ [`r t2_target_q2.5`, `r t2_target_q97.5`];
t3: $M=$ `r t3_target_m`,
$95\%~\text{CrI}=$ [`r t3_target_q2.5`, `r t3_target_q97.5`]). Fixations to the competitor in the Early competition condition are higher early and decrease in the third and fourth time windows (t0: $M=$ `r t0_comp_coh_m`, 
$95\%~\text{CrI}=$ [`r t0_comp_coh_q2.5`, `r t0_comp_coh_q97.5`]; 
t1: $M=$ `r t1_comp_coh_m`, 
$95\%~\text{CrI}=$ [`r t1_comp_coh_q2.5`, `r t1_comp_coh_q97.5`];
t2: $M=$ `r t2_comp_coh_m`, 
$95\%~\text{CrI}=$ [`r t2_comp_coh_q2.5`, `r t2_comp_coh_q97.5`];
t3: $M=$ `r t3_comp_coh_m`,
$95\%~\text{CrI}=$ [`r t3_comp_coh_q2.5`, `r t3_comp_coh_q97.5`]), while those in the Late competition condition remain elevated in the latest time window (t0: $M=$ `r t0_comp_rhy_m`, 
$95\%~\text{CrI}=$ [`r t0_comp_rhy_q2.5`, `r t0_comp_rhy_q97.5`]; 
t1: $M=$ `r t1_comp_rhy_m`, 
$95\%~\text{CrI}=$ [`r t1_comp_rhy_q2.5`, `r t1_comp_rhy_q97.5`];
t2: $M=$ `r t2_comp_rhy_m`, 
$95\%~\text{CrI}=$ [`r t2_comp_rhy_q2.5`, `r t2_comp_rhy_q97.5`];
t3: $M=$ `r t3_comp_rhy_m`,
$95\%~\text{CrI}=$ [`r t3_comp_rhy_q2.5`, `r t3_comp_rhy_q97.5`]). 

To quantify how much competitors capture attention in different conditions and time windows, I calculate the posterior estimate of the target advantage as the proportion of fixations to the target minus the proportion of fixations to the competitor or one of the distractors. Greater target advantage indicates more attention to the target relative to the competitor or distractor (i.e., less competition). Across conditions and blocks, the model predicts that the target advantage increases as the stimulus unfolded (t0: $M=$ `r t0_TA_m`, 
$95\%~\text{CrI}=$ [`r t0_TA_q2.5`, `r t0_TA_q97.5`]; 
t1: $M=$ `r t1_TA_m`, 
$95\%~\text{CrI}=$ [`r t1_TA_q2.5`, `r t1_TA_q97.5`];
t2: $M=$ `r t2_TA_m`, 
$95\%~\text{CrI}=$ [`r t2_TA_q2.5`, `r t2_TA_q97.5`];
t3: $M=$ `r t3_TA_m`,
$95\%~\text{CrI}=$ [`r t3_TA_q2.5`, `r t3_TA_q97.5`]).
In the pre-noun onset time window (t0), the target advantage does not differ by condition ($\Delta_{\text{Early - No Compet.}}=$ `r t0_TA_coh_minus_no_comp_m`,
$95\%~\text{CrI}_{\text{Early - No Compet.}}=$ [`r t0_TA_coh_minus_no_comp_q2.5`, `r t0_TA_coh_minus_no_comp_q97.5`],
$\Delta_{\text{Late - No Compet.}}=$ `r t0_TA_rhy_minus_no_comp_m`,
$95\%~\text{CrI}_{\text{Late - No Compet.}}=$ [`r t0_TA_rhy_minus_no_comp_q2.5`, `r t0_TA_rhy_minus_no_comp_q97.5`]). 
In the second time window (t1), the target advantage is more likely to be larger in the No Competition condition than in the Early competition condition ($\Delta_{\text{Early - No Compet.}}=$ `r t1_TA_coh_minus_no_comp_m`,
$95\%~\text{CrI}_{\text{Early - No Compet.}}=$ [`r t1_TA_coh_minus_no_comp_q2.5`, `r t1_TA_coh_minus_no_comp_q97.5`]
) or the Late Competition condition ($\Delta_{\text{Late - No Compet.}}=$ `r t1_TA_rhy_minus_no_comp_m`,
$95\%~\text{CrI}_{\text{Late - No Compet.}}=$ [`r t1_TA_rhy_minus_no_comp_q2.5`, `r t1_TA_rhy_minus_no_comp_q97.5`]), indicating competition from both early and late competitors in this window. The target advantage was reduced in the Early Competition condition relative to the Late Competition condition ($\Delta_{\text{Early - Late}}=$ `r t1_TA_coh_minus_rhy_comp_m`,
$95\%~\text{CrI}_{\text{Early - Late}}=$ [`r t1_TA_coh_minus_rhy_comp_q2.5`, `r t1_TA_coh_minus_rhy_comp_q97.5`]), indicating greater competition from the early competitors in this window.
In the third time window (t2), the target advantage is more likely to be larger in the No Competition condition than in the Early competition condition ($\Delta_{\text{Early - No Compet.}}=$ `r t2_TA_coh_minus_no_comp_m`,
$95\%~\text{CrI}_{\text{Early - No Compet.}}=$ [`r t2_TA_coh_minus_no_comp_q2.5`, `r t2_TA_coh_minus_no_comp_q97.5`]
) or the Late Competition condition ($\Delta_{\text{Late - No Compet.}}=$ `r t2_TA_rhy_minus_no_comp_m`,
$95\%~\text{CrI}_{\text{Late - No Compet.}}=$ [`r t2_TA_rhy_minus_no_comp_q2.5`, `r t2_TA_rhy_minus_no_comp_q97.5`]).
The target advantage was nominally increased in the Early Competition condition relative to the Late Competition condition ($\Delta_{\text{Early - Late}}=$ `r t2_TA_coh_minus_rhy_comp_m`,
$95\%~\text{CrI}_{\text{Early - Late}}=$ [`r t2_TA_coh_minus_rhy_comp_q2.5`, `r t2_TA_coh_minus_rhy_comp_q97.5`]), indicating similar competition from the early and late competitors in this window.
Finally, in the fourth time window (t3), the target advantage is more likely to be greater in the No Competition condition than in the Early competition condition ($\Delta_{\text{Early - No Compet.}}=$ `r t3_TA_coh_minus_no_comp_m`,
$95\%~\text{CrI}_{\text{Early - No Compet.}}=$ [`r t3_TA_coh_minus_no_comp_q2.5`, `r t3_TA_coh_minus_no_comp_q97.5`]) and the Late Competition condition ($\Delta_{\text{Late - No Compet.}}=$ `r t3_TA_rhy_minus_no_comp_m`,
$95\%~\text{CrI}_{\text{Late - No Compet.}}=$ [`r t3_TA_rhy_minus_no_comp_q2.5`, `r t3_TA_rhy_minus_no_comp_q97.5`]). 
The target advantage was increased in the Early Competition condition relative to the Late Competition condition ($\Delta_{\text{Early - Late}}=$ `r t3_TA_coh_minus_rhy_comp_m`,
$95\%~\text{CrI}_{\text{Early - Late}}=$ [`r t3_TA_coh_minus_rhy_comp_q2.5`, `r t3_TA_coh_minus_rhy_comp_q97.5`]), indicating greater competition from the late competitors in this window.
In sum, the posterior estimates capture the critical patterns observed in the eye-tracking data (Figure\ \@ref(fig:model-posteriors-plots)E).


## Listeners adapt to the noise in the environment 


```{r pulling tau values for text}
tau_summary = fit_avg_g$summary(variables = c("tau[1]", "tau[2]", "tau[3]", "tau[4]", "tau[5]"),
                                "mean", 
                                "sd", 
                                ~posterior::quantile2(.x, probs = c(0.025, 0.975)),
                                "rhat", 
                                "ess_bulk") %>% 
  mutate(
    across(where(is.numeric), ~ round(.x, digits = 3))
    )

tau1_m = tau_summary %>% filter(variable == "tau[1]") %>% pull(mean) 
tau1_q2.5 = tau_summary %>% filter(variable == "tau[1]") %>% pull(q2.5) 
tau1_q97.5 = tau_summary %>% filter(variable == "tau[1]") %>% pull(q97.5)

tau2_q2.5 = tau_summary %>% filter(variable == "tau[2]") %>% pull(q2.5) 
tau2_q97.5 = tau_summary %>% filter(variable == "tau[2]") %>% pull(q97.5)

tau3_q2.5 = tau_summary %>% filter(variable == "tau[3]") %>% pull(q2.5) 
tau3_q97.5 = tau_summary %>% filter(variable == "tau[3]") %>% pull(q97.5) 

tau4_m = tau_summary %>% filter(variable == "tau[4]") %>% pull(mean) 
tau4_q2.5 = tau_summary %>% filter(variable == "tau[4]") %>% pull(q2.5) 
tau4_q97.5 = tau_summary %>% filter(variable == "tau[4]") %>% pull(q97.5) 

tau5_m = tau_summary %>% filter(variable == "tau[5]") %>% pull(mean) 
tau5_q2.5 = tau_summary %>% filter(variable == "tau[5]") %>% pull(q2.5) 
tau5_q97.5 = tau_summary %>% filter(variable == "tau[5]") %>% pull(q97.5) 

tau_contrasts_summary = fit_avg_g$summary(variables = c(
  "initial_noise_effect", 
  "noise_residual_effect",
  "noise_contrast_effect",
  "explain_away_effect",
  "explained_noise_residual_effect"), 
  "mean",
  "sd", 
  ~posterior::quantile2(.x, probs = c(0.025, 0.975)),
  "rhat", 
  "ess_bulk") %>% 
  mutate(
    across(where(is.numeric), ~ round(.x, digits = 3))
    )

initial_noise_effect_m = tau_contrasts_summary %>% filter(variable == "initial_noise_effect") %>% pull(mean) 
initial_noise_effect_q2.5 = tau_contrasts_summary %>% filter(variable == "initial_noise_effect") %>% pull(q2.5) 
initial_noise_effect_q97.5 = tau_contrasts_summary %>% filter(variable == "initial_noise_effect") %>% pull(q97.5) 

noise_residual_effect_m = tau_contrasts_summary %>% filter(variable == "noise_residual_effect") %>% pull(mean) 
noise_residual_effect_q2.5 = tau_contrasts_summary %>% filter(variable == "noise_residual_effect") %>% pull(q2.5) 
noise_residual_effect_q97.5 = tau_contrasts_summary %>% filter(variable == "noise_residual_effect") %>% pull(q97.5)

noise_contrast_effect_q97.5 = tau_contrasts_summary %>% filter(variable == "noise_contrast_effect") %>% pull(q97.5) 

explain_away_effect_m = tau_contrasts_summary %>% filter(variable == "explain_away_effect") %>% pull(mean) 
explain_away_effect_q2.5 = tau_contrasts_summary %>% filter(variable == "explain_away_effect") %>% pull(q2.5) 
explain_away_effect_q97.5 = tau_contrasts_summary %>% filter(variable == "explain_away_effect") %>% pull(q97.5) 

explained_noise_residual_effect_m = tau_contrasts_summary %>% filter(variable == "explained_noise_residual_effect") %>% pull(mean)

explained_noise_residual_effect_q97.5 = tau_contrasts_summary %>% filter(variable == "explained_noise_residual_effect") %>% pull(q97.5) 
```


In addition to demonstrating that the competition condition effects are well captured by a Bayesian noisy-channel model, analysis of the posterior reveals that listeners adapt their estimate of the noise probability, $\tau$, in response to the noise in the environment, based on multiple sources of information. Figure\ \@ref(fig:tau-effects-plots)A summarizes
the posterior predictions of the timecourse of fixation proportions to targets and competitors across competition conditions, comparing all *Intact* blocks and *Noisy* blocks. Added noise in fillers decreases fixations to the target across competition conditions suggesting that $\tau$ is lower in the *Intact* blocks. 

The posterior estimates of $\tau$ values by block type and contrasts between blocks are summarized in Figures\ \@ref(fig:tau-effects-plots)B and C. The lowest $\tau$ is observed in the first *Intact* block which did not contain added noise on filler trials ($M=$ `r apa_num(tau1_m, digits = 3)`, 
$95\%~\text{CrI}=$ [`r apa_num(tau1_q2.5, digits = 3)`, `r apa_num(tau1_q97.5, digits = 3)`]). The highest $\tau$ is observed in the first *Noisy* block ($M=$ `r apa_num(tau2_m, digits = 3)`, 
$95\%~\text{CrI}=$ [`r apa_num(tau2_q2.5, digits = 3)`, `r apa_num(tau2_q97.5, digits = 3)`],
$\Delta=$ `r apa_num(initial_noise_effect_m, digits = 3)`,
$95\%~\text{CrI}=$ [`r apa_num(initial_noise_effect_q2.5, digits = 3)`, `r apa_num(initial_noise_effect_q97.5, digits = 3)`]), indicating that listeners increase their noise estimates when there is an elevated frequency of acoustic noise in their environment. 
$\tau$ was higher for the *Intact* block when it was preceded by a *Noisy* block ($M=$ `r apa_num(tau4_m, digits = 3)`, 
$95\%~\text{CrI}=$ [`r apa_num(tau4_q2.5, digits = 3)`, `r apa_num(tau4_q97.5, digits = 3)`],
$\Delta=$ `r apa_num(noise_residual_effect_m, digits = 3)`,
$95\%~\text{CrI}=$ [`r apa_num(noise_residual_effect_q2.5, digits = 3)`, `r apa_num(noise_residual_effect_q97.5, digits = 3)`]) suggesting that the estimate of noise is based on continuous perceptual evidence accumulation. Similarly, $\tau$ was lower for the *Noisy* block when it was preceded by an *Intact* block ($M=$ `r apa_num(tau3_m, digits = 3)`, 
$95\%~\text{CrI}=$ [`r apa_num(tau3_q2.5, digits = 3)`, `r apa_num(tau3_q97.5, digits = 3)`],
$\Delta=$ `r apa_num(noise_contrast_effect_m, digits = 3)`,
$95\%~\text{CrI}=$ [`r apa_num(noise_contrast_effect_q2.5, digits = 3)`, `r apa_num(noise_contrast_effect_q97.5, digits = 3)`]). Finally, $\tau$ was lower for the *Intact* block preceded by a *Noisy* block if the participant was explicitly informed that there was an error in the previous block and that the following set of stimuli would not contain acoustic noise ($M=$ `r apa_num(tau5_m, digits = 3)`, 
$95\%~\text{CrI}=$ [`r apa_num(tau5_q2.5, digits = 3)`, `r apa_num(tau5_q97.5, digits = 3)`],
$\Delta=$ `r apa_num(explain_away_effect_m, digits = 3)`,
$95\%~\text{CrI}=$ [`r apa_num(explain_away_effect_q2.5, digits = 3)`, `r apa_num(explain_away_effect_q97.5, digits = 3)`]). In addition to accumulating perceptual evidence, listeners can also flexibly update their noise estimates based on a verbal characterization, which "explains away" the presence of noise.
